newsitem.title: INDIA: India warns of foreign meddling in Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: India warns of foreign meddling in Afghanistan.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma said that continuing conflict in Afghanistan was of great concern to both India and Kazakhstan and warned against foreign interference.
"A current development of great concern to both our countries is the continuing conflict in Afghanistan," Sharma said in a speech made available to reporters on Monday.
He was due to make the speech at a banquet in honour of visiting Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev later on Monday.
Sharma called for dialogue between warring groups in Afghanistan and said India was committed to the stability, unity and territorial integrity of the nation.
He called for an end to foreign interference in the country.
"We share your concern that violations of those principles would adversely affect the entire region," Sharma told the Kazakh president. "There is no military solution to the Afghan conflict."

The Islamic purist Taleban movement has taken over most of Afghanistan, including the capital Kabul, but has met stiff resistance from an alliance between former government troops and ethnic Uzbek forces.
India accuses arch-foe Pakistan of aiding Taleban warriors and of interfering in Afghanistan's internal affairs. Pakistan says it is neutral.
Sharma said India fully supported efforts by the United Nations to end the fighting in Afghanistan through negotiation between warring groups.
Nazarbayev earlier told reporters that Central Asian republics were opposed to the spread of Moslem fundamentalism in the region, in an apparent reference to the Taleban warriors.
